Under v4's own A1 logic, baselines marked it [~] before the first README write in 26 of 37 trials. The most recent no-skill preflight, 20260930-105529, did it in 3 of 3, and I confirmed that by reading all three transcripts. summary: I agree with the reviser: do not spend the preflight. The scored behavior, marking a pending task with real work [~] before doing it, is something the baseline without the skill already does unprompted. The latest preflight did it 3/3, selectively: it skipped [~] on the no-work task and claimed the real-work one, and across the full pool the rate is 26/37. Removing the reclaim clause and T2's [!] leaves the CHANGELOG task in the position where the baseline claims about 70% of the time, so the k=3 preflight would most likely BLOCK. Even if it passed, k=5 needs a baseline at or below 1/5 to read IMPROVED. I found no honest alternative design for this assertion. The skill's distinguishing claim (SKILL.md:92 "Mark `[~]` before starting a task ... so a crash leaves the file honest"; :102 "1. Mark it `[~]`.") matches what the baseline already does. A treatment would pass, but there is no gap to measure. Actions for the orchestrator or user: reset or drop branch test/eval-redesign-executing-verify. It still points at ee2e5919 in <worktree>/rd-executing, and the reviser's `git reset --hard main` was denied. Revert the dirty package-lock.json. Record the ceiling finding in evals/skill-eval-coverage.md and the decision log through their owners. If v4 is ever revived, its unresolved write-detection regex defect (line 196) must be fixed first.
